# Temple Scroll Column 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 36 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**36:1** Set aside areas east of the temple city, away from it, for people with skin diseases.

**36:2** They must live there alone and may not enter the temple city.

**36:3** Set aside areas north of the temple city for anyone with a bodily discharge — whether a chronic condition or a seminal emission.

**36:4** They must stay there until they are purified; they may not enter the temple city while they are unclean.

**36:5** Set aside an area west of the temple city for women during their menstrual periods.

**36:6** They must not enter My temple city or contaminate it — for I dwell there.

**36:7** I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel forever and always.

**36:8** Anyone who has recovered from a skin disease must bring the required purification offering before he may enter the temple city.

**36:9** A priest shall examine him outside the city, and if the disease is gone, the priest shall declare him clean.

**36:10** On the eighth day he shall present his guilt offering, his sin offering, and his burnt offering as prescribed.

**36:11** When a man with a discharge finds that it has stopped, he must count seven days for his purification.

**36:12** On the eighth day he must wash his clothes and bathe his whole body in running water; then he will be clean.

**36:13** After that he may enter the temple city and bring his offering to the LORD — two turtledoves or two young pigeons: one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.

**36:14** The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge, and he will be clean.

**36:15** The Israelites must keep away from all impurity and must not defile the land where I live.

**36:16** For I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel, and the land shall be holy.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column creates three quarantine zones around the temple city for different types of ritual impurity. The purification procedures draw on Leviticus 13-15 but apply to the entire city, not just the sanctuary. The repeated emphasis on divine dwelling motivates the strict spatial separation.*
